newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-Juppe says to step down, whoever wins.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Juppe says to step down, whoever wins.

text.p: Following are market comments following an announcement by Prime Minister Alain Juppe that he would step down whichever party wins the second round of France's parliamentary election on Sunday.
JEAN-PIERRE FILBIEN, EQUITIES DIRECTOR, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL
It will be well received by the markets. They believed that Juppe was finished.
I think that people have made a protest vote. With Juppe gone, the centre-right has a better chance in the runoff.
IAIN LINDSAY, BOND ANALYST, CREDIT LYONNAIS

It must be mildly positive. I don't think it will make a big difference to the result. There will be other things that will be much more decisive. From the beginning the campaign platform has been based on the (policy) programme and not the personalities.

The market reaction will depend on who will replace Juppe. It may be (National Assembly speaker) Philippe Seguin, who is a popular choice but not the market's choice. He is ambigious on Maastricht, pro-growth and less rigorous on public deficits.
European markets might suffer as a consequence.

On the more liiberal path there is (former prime minister Edouard) Balladur or (former budget minister Nicolas) Sarkozy which is more positive. The most positive is (former finance minsiter) Alain Madelin who is the most pro-business of the liberals.
It's an important strategic choice by the right to determine whether to go for market liberal policies and free-entreprise or reassure social protection will be maintained.
